beats: Nobody brings a bigger crane. Tower cranes build themselves taller.
It lifts its own head and slides a new piece of tower underneath.
Near the top, a steel cage hugs the tower, with a hydraulic jack inside.
Workers unbolt the top. Now everything above rests on one jack.
So it must balance: the trolley rolls out until both arms even out.
Then the jack pushes the whole top upward: cab, arm, motors, counterweight.
A gap opens in the cage, one section tall: up to six metres, twenty feet.
The next section waits on a rail, lifted there by the crane's own hook.
It rolls into the gap, and the top is bolted back onto it.
Section by section, the crane climbs with the building it's helping to build.
So that crane didn't arrive that tall. It climbed there, one piece at a time.
Cogwise: how things work. Follow for the next one!
